slices.label: Adjacency-matrix random-greedy-MIS size estimation
slices.task: Estimate the size of the random greedy MIS induced by an algorithm-generated random vertex permutation
assumptions: Adjacency-matrix bit oracle on an n-vertex graph
Returns one scalar estimate, not an explicit MIS or the expectation over permutations

yAxis.label: Adjacency-matrix query exponent p in Õ(n^p)

parameters.plotInterpretation: x=1 is the limiting boundary for every fixed ε>0; y is the n-exponent and suppresses the ε^-2 factor.
parameters.coordinateConvention: Fix ε=1/4 for the displayed coordinate; the formula Õ(n^{3/2}/ε²) and RGMIS output definition remain in the table.

results.bound: Õ(n^(3/2)/ε²) time and at most that many adjacency-matrix queries
results.guarantee: Purely multiplicative (1+ε) approximation to |RGMIS(π)| for a generated random permutation π, with high probability
results.sourceLocation: Theorem 1.3; Section 3.3 and note following Algorithm 4
results.notes: The π-specific cardinality is a randomized choice of valid maximal independent set size. Not maximum independent set size, not a fixed externally specified MIS, and not Eπ|RGMIS(π)|. Numeric frontier intentionally omitted because epsilon and task semantics are not common to construction slices. Plot uses x=1 as the limiting boundary for any fixed ε>0 and y=3/2 for the n-exponent; the ε^-2 factor remains in the bound.

slices.label: Adjacency-matrix explicit construction
slices.task: Output the vertex set of an explicit maximal independent set

results.guarantee: Explicit maximal independent set, even with one randomly located edge
results.notes: The paper gives the one-random-edge hard example. This is for full construction and must not be placed on the size-estimation frontier.

papers.title: Sublinear Metric Steiner Forest via Maximal Independent Set
